blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-3 (Dropped deliveries are logged only at debug level, through console) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Wait between attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s…), or better, hand failed deliveries to a queue retried over minutes; a merchant endpoint that is down for a few seconds otherwise exhausts all five attempts at once and the event is lost.
findings.title: Retries fire back to back, with no backoff

findings.recommendation: Log the response status (and event id, attempt) when it is not ok, and stop retrying on non-retryable statuses (4xx other than 408/429); today a 404 or 401 from the merchant is retried five times and leaves no trace of why the delivery failed.
findings.title: Every non-2xx response is retried and never logged

findings.recommendation: The per-attempt failure at line 21 is logged the same way. Use the project's structured logger (`src/logger.ts`, as `src/events.ts` does) with fields (eventId, merchant, attempt, status, error), log the final drop at error level, and emit a delivery-failure metric; as written, a merchant that never receives a settled-payment notification goes unnoticed in production, where debug output is normally filtered.
findings.title: Dropped deliveries are logged only at debug level, through console

findings.recommendation: Do not await delivery inside the listener — enqueue it (outbox table or job queue) and deliver asynchronously; `publish` in `src/events.ts` awaits each listener in turn, so a slow or down merchant endpoint (5 attempts × 5 s timeout) stalls the payment service's publish path and every listener after this one.
findings.title: Delivery runs inline in the payment event publish, blocking it for up to ~25 s

findings.recommendation: Register the listener behind a configuration flag read from the environment (e.g. `WEBHOOKS_ENABLED`), so operators can stop outgoing calls to merchants — for instance during a retry storm — without rolling back the release.
findings.title: No switch to turn webhooks off without a redeploy

findings.recommendation: Read the attempt limit and the request timeout (`AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` at line 15) from configuration, with these values as defaults, so they can be tuned without a release.
findings.title: Timeout and attempt limit are hard-coded
